clue.text: Little bit of affair — maybe croon about it

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to croon is one way to sing, hence the 'maybe'
an affair is a matter, as in 'a private matter'

explanation.surface: A snippet of gossip about an affair, perhaps sung about by a crooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight superficial amount, such as a little knowledge of a language.

clue.text: Army left with powder no good for fighting!

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
cum is Latin for with, as in 'kitchen-cum-dining-room'

explanation.surface: A soldier complains that the powder issued is useless in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on gunpowder: this is a powder for the body, quite useless on a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum is a soft toiletry dusting powder, so it is a powder with no military use.

clue.text: Various meals out with close buddy

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the following words take different arrangements

explanation.surface: Going out for a range of meals with a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A soulmate is a person one is deeply close to, an intimate friend.

clue.text: Male tucking into rotten organic stuff, a sort of dip

indicators.note: tucking into means placing one thing inside another

parts.note: humus is decayed vegetable matter in soil

explanation.surface: A man eating something putrid, which turns out to be a type of dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hummus is a Middle Eastern chickpea purée eaten as a dip.

clue.text: Noise of bells leads to a fight

explanation.surface: Church bells ring out and set off a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase imitates the chime of bells and is also informal British slang for a heated quarrel.

clue.text: What sounds like a foreign city ramble

indicators.note: these words say the letters entered are pronounced like the place named

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital, foreign to a British setter

explanation.surface: A question about wandering around a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander about aimlessly, a synonym of ramble as a verb.

clue.text: Pain would get learner going to uni doc in the past

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
U is short for university
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
ago means in the past, as in 'years ago'

explanation.surface: A student visiting the university doctor long ago complains of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back.

clue.text: Bizarre dream with trollops and 'unspiritual' peers

indicators.note: bizarre means strange or twisted, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A peculiar dream involving loose women and worldly nobles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords Temporal are the secular members of the House of Lords, as opposed to the bishops who are the Lords Spiritual.

clue.text: School attire needed when one is in a French class

indicators.note: is in tells us one item sits inside the others

parts.note: un is French for a
a form is a school class
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Clothing required for a French lesson at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A uniform is the standard dress pupils must wear at many schools.

clue.text: Underground worker changes having drunk whisky and, initially, non-alcoholic drinks

parts.note: a miner works below ground

indicators.note: having drunk means taking something inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A miner, after some whisky, switches to soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral waters are bottled spring waters, drinks containing no alcohol.

clue.text: Network offering 'Culture' — I'm excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An arts network promising thrilling culture.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticulum is a netlike structure, from the Latin for a little net.

clue.text: Good African dictator once a street urchin

parts.note: Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A former African tyrant was once a child of the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamin is a French-derived word for a street urchin, a neglected child of the streets.

clue.text: Within dam there's a source of power

indicators.note: within says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to dam a flow is to stem it

explanation.surface: Inside a dam lies a supply of power, as in hydroelectricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' looks like a noun but is the verb, to stem a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam drives turbines and engines, a classic source of mechanical power.

clue.text: Sailor needs helper — not the first English person to do a bunk

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: not the first says the earliest instance of the letter is removed

parts.note: a seconder supports a motion, a helper

explanation.surface: A sailor needs an assistant, though not an English one, to run off.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do a bunk' is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: An absconder is someone who runs off secretly, which is what doing a bunk means.

clue.text: Top gallery? I walked up to get to it

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: I paced is another way of saying I walked
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Climbing to the highest gallery on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for killing them, here by cutting off the head.

clue.text: Essence of Eastern book about Greek character

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: The core of an Eastern text concerning a Greek figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect embodiment, the essence of a quality.

clue.text: Rate poet awful as provider of light entertainment

indicators.note: awful means bad, so the letters are taken as badly arranged

explanation.surface: Judge a poet dreadful as an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera, a form of light entertainment.

clue.text: Charming visitors at Christmas (short visit)

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men who visited the infant Jesus

indicators.note: short means a word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a call is a short visit

explanation.surface: Christmas visitors whose brief stay was delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Magical means enchanting, a synonym of charming.

clue.text: Examinations made by detectives turning up to interrupt dinners maybe

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: dinners are an example of meals

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives arriving to break up dinners carry out examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicals are physical examinations by a doctor.

clue.text: Stubborn Prince, conceited leader being deposed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is thrown out, as a deposed leader is

parts.note: bigheaded means conceited

explanation.surface: An obstinate, vain prince loses his throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigheaded means obstinate and stubborn.

clue.text: Duke and stranger ramble in talk

parts.note: odder means stranger

explanation.surface: A duke and an odd fellow wander on in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to totter or potter feebly, here rambling in speech.

clue.text: Brown animals heading west across island

indicators.note: across says one piece lies over and around another
in an across clue heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: apes are animals

explanation.surface: Brown creatures travelling west over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Introduction to show with an instrument providing welcome

indicators.note: introduction to means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A show opens with music played to greet the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a gesture of greeting or welcome.

clue.text: Show always being brought back — enthralling for all the family?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece holds another
brought back means read backwards

parts.note: ever means always
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A show that keeps returning and entertains the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light theatrical show of sketches and songs.

clue.text: Time very short for rising star

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards

parts.note: an age is a period of time
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A brief moment for a star on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Volume of claret I'd drunk? End of life would follow!

indicators.note: would follow puts the next piece after the first
drunk means wobbly, so the letters are jumbled
end of means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Drinking that much claret would kill you.
explanation.definitionFit: A decalitre is a metric unit of volume, ten litres.

clue.text: One who's left something in shelter outside entrance

indicators.note: outside means placed around the other piece

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a shelter by a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left something' suggests leaving behind; it means being bequeathed something.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a bequest in a will.

clue.text: Understatement in stories about small child

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: stories can mean lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Understatement in tales about a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a rhetorical figure of understatement, as in 'not bad'.
